description:
Welcome to team AetherLabs! We are a group of developers and space enthusiasts passionate about software engineering, problem-solving, and game design. With solid experience in building cross-platform applications, writing clean backend code, and designing engaging mechanics, we are ready to take on innovative challenges.

We are currently exploring various challenges to build an immersive and impactful project that connects technology with the wonders of our universe.
summary: Spacecraft fire researchers need to find which experiments measured the conditions they are investigating. We built Flame Filters to make that evidence easier to find and compare. Researchers can filter NASA combustion experiments by fuel, measurement, and test conditions, then trace ranked results to test records and report pages. Our prototype covers BASS-II experiments on solid materials and FLEX experiments on liquid fuel droplets. The dashboard flags missing measurements and unconfirmed units so researchers can judge what the available evidence supports.
details: Flame Filters organizes NASA PSI test tables into JSON records that preserve test identifiers, conditions, and measurements. Python and Flask calculate how closely investigations match the selected filters. The system uses pypdf to extract relevant report passages and retain their page numbers. Gemini interprets the shortlisted evidence, while comparison tables and Recharts visualizations use recorded measurements. React and TypeScript power the interface. The public showcase replays a recorded query so judges can explore the results and trace them to NASA sources without an API key. Source code: https://github.com/hazem-codes/Flame-In-FireFall. Gemini assisted with scientific summaries and interpretations, and we use OpenAI Codex assisted with softwere verification. The NASA measurements are sourced from the original investigations.
